system_description.narrative_title: Energy, Finance and Geopolitics in a Fracturing Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is in multi-domain flux: kinetic wars and regional crisis (Ukraine, Middle East, maritime flashpoints) are producing acute energy shocks that governments meet with emergency reserves and political pressure. Those shocks coincide with a global financial stress event—sharp bond sell-offs, rising yields and currency moves—which constrain central banks and fiscal space and amplify domestic political risks through inflation and volatile markets. Simultaneously, great-power competition and strategic industrial shifts (chips, data centers, electrification and EV supply chains) are reconfiguring leverage between states and firms, creating cascading interdependencies across security, energy and finance.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances; active armed conflicts and military postures; global energy flows, fuel reserves and commodity markets; sovereign debt and global bond markets, central banks and monetary policy; multinational firms and strategic supply chains (chips, data centres, autos, LNG); electoral politics and domestic policy decisions that feed back into international relations.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-security system (the globalized Anthropocene political-economic order incorporating climate and resource constraints)
adjacent_subsystems: International energy markets & emergency reserve mechanisms
Global fixed-income and FX financial markets
Great-power military competition across Europe, Middle East and Indo-Pacific
Global technology & industrial supply chains (chips, AI/data centres, EVs)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with Western backers, are locked in an intensifying conventional and hybrid war as Moscow adopts harsher tactics and Kyiv fields new weapons and strikes.

variables.name: Iran‑Middle East confrontation
variables.description: Iran, regional states and external powers are engaged in escalating military and diplomatic confrontation that is imperilling shipping routes, regional security and is provoking wider deployments.

variables.name: US‑China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI and strategic supply chains through export controls, investment moves and trade diplomacy, reshaping global tech governance.

variables.name: Global energy and fuel shock
variables.description: World fuel and energy markets are experiencing acute supply shocks and price volatility driven by conflict-related disruptions and coordinated reserve releases, forcing policy interventions and reallocations.

variables.name: Global sovereign bond‑market stress
variables.description: Developed- and emerging-market sovereign debt markets are undergoing a sustained sell-off and rising yields that are constraining fiscal room, altering investor flows and pressuring monetary policy choices.
